answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed reputation that decays: every agent must lock a small, slashable deposit before it can transact, and that deposit only gains weight through a history of useful, verified work. A fresh identity starts in a nebula of untrusted newcomers, unable to reach the haven of high-value deals until its signal — completed tasks, honest attestations, no disputes — proves it over time. Sybils can spawn thousands of accounts, but each one must pay the deposit and wait out the same slow climb, so flooding the network costs more than it can ever earn.
